html:
Suryavarman II was king of the Khmer Empire from 1113 until about 1150, and the builder of Angkor Wat, the largest religious monument in the world.

He came to power by defeating a rival king, and reunited an empire that had split. He restored strong central government and sent embassies to Song China, renewing contact with the Chinese court. He fought many wars: against Đại Việt to the east, which failed, and against Champa, where his armies took the Cham capital for a while.

His great work was Angkor Wat, dedicated to Vishnu rather than to Shiva, as most earlier royal temples were. Its long galleries of reliefs show scenes from Hindu epics and a procession of the king himself with his army. It probably served as his funeral temple; it faces west, the direction linked with death. His posthumous name, Paramavishnuloka, means "he who has gone to the world of Vishnu". After his death the empire weakened until Jayavarman VII restored it.
